message.reasoning_content:
need to determine appropriate crime(s) for the facts. The facts: a public servant (闵某) who was a director (主任) of a public apartment (公寓) and also of a housing construction life segment (房建生活段). He used his position to embezzle public funds: 1) with others, set up bonus distribution schemes to siphon off 64,000 yuan from off-book funds, personally got 25,500 yuan. 2) From Dec 2012 to June 2014, used his position in procurement, used false invoices to defraud public funds, 8 times, total 15,350 yuan. Total embezzlement 79,350 yuan, personally got 40,850 yuan. He is main participant, principal.

Thus crime: 贪污罪 (embezzlement) for public officials. Since he is a public servant (state employee) and used position to embezzle public funds, the correct charge is "贪污罪". Possibly also "受贿罪"? No, he didn't receive bribes, he embezzled. So only 贪污.

But sometimes Chinese law distinguishes between 贪污罪 (embezzlement) and 受贿罪 (bribery). Here it's embezzlement. Also "挪用公款罪" is for non-public officials? Actually 挪用公款 is for state employees who misappropriate public funds for personal use, but not necessarily with the element of abuse of position? In Chinese criminal law, 贪污罪 applies to state functionaries who misappropriate public property. 挪用公款罪 applies to state employees who misappropriate public funds for personal use, but not necessarily with the element of misappropriation of public property? Actually both are similar. The difference: 贪污罪 is for state functionaries who misappropriate public property (including money, goods). 挪用公款罪 is for state employees who misappropriate public funds (money) for personal use, but not for property? The case includes both money and procurement fraud. Usually the charge is 贪污罪. The description says "共同贪污" and "个人贪污". So definitely 贪污.

Thus answer: [罪名]贪污<eoa>

Check if any other charges: maybe "滥用职权" (abuse of power) but that's not a separate crime, it's a circumstance. The prosecution mentions "××××、××××、××××" maybe referencing articles for 贪污罪, maybe also "受贿罪"? But not.

Thus final answer: 贪污.
